evals.name: python-flask-orders-review
evals.prompt: Please do an SSEM-style securability review of this Python Flask order-handling module. It's part of a B2C customer portal. I want the full SSEM scorecard with per-attribute scores, the three-part report, and the evaluation checklist. Be specific about what's broken — engineering improvements, not generic 'follow best practices' advice. The file is attached.

assertions.text: Output contains the three-part SSEM report (Score Summary / Detailed Findings / Appendix A checklist) with all three parts present and clearly labeled

All ten FIASSE v1.1 SSEM attributes (Analyzability, Modifiability, Testability, Observability, Confidentiality, Accountability, Authenticity, Availability, Integrity, Resilience) each have a numeric 0-10 score, or an explicit 'Not assessed' / 'N/A' marker
Attribute scores show meaningful differentiation — not all the same number — reflecting the mixed quality of the code under review

The overall score is computed as min(raw mean of the ten attributes, lowest attribute + 3.0), and the report shows the raw mean, the floor, which constraint is binding, and the weakest attribute by name
Attributes are weighted equally at 1/10 each; pillar scores, if reported, are labeled as diagnostics and are not used to compute the overall score
A grade from the six-band scale (Exemplary/Strong/Adequate/Weak/Minimal/Absent) is produced consistent with the overall score
The report states that the SSEM score is a directional management aid and not a statement of assurance, compliance, or security (FIASSE v1.1 SA.4)
SQL injection in get_order via string concatenation is flagged with a specific code reference and remediation
Hardcoded DB_PASSWORD secret is flagged with a specific code reference and remediation
create_order accepting a client-supplied user_id is flagged as an Isolated Integrity violation (FIASSE v1.1 S4.4.1.2), not by the retired name 'Derived Integrity'
Lack of structured logging (use of print() and limited audit fields) is flagged under Accountability and/or Observability
Lack of tests ("No tests in this module yet") is flagged under Testability
Every finding carries a severity (CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW/INFO) and is tagged as either systemic or local
Every expected improvement is expressed in attribute points against a named attribute (e.g. '+5.0 on Integrity'), never as a bare point value
Appendix A includes a 50-item checklist (5 items for each of the ten attributes: 20 Maintainability, 15 Trustworthiness, 15 Reliability) with pass/fail markers and a summary count

evals.name: node-express-tickets-review
evals.prompt: Run a securable-engineering review of this Express/TypeScript helpdesk-tickets file. Score it through SSEM, give me the three-part report, and call out the engineering work that needs to happen before we'd consider this audit-ready. File is attached.

assertions.text: Output contains the three-part SSEM report (Score Summary / Detailed Findings / Appendix A checklist) with all three parts present
All ten FIASSE v1.1 SSEM attributes each have a numeric 0-10 score, or an explicit 'Not assessed' / 'N/A' marker
Scores show meaningful differentiation across attributes (not uniform)
The overall score is computed as min(raw mean, lowest attribute + 3.0) with the raw mean, floor, binding constraint, and weakest attribute all shown
The report answers the 'audit-ready' framing in posture terms and states plainly that an SSEM score is not an assurance or compliance verdict (FIASSE v1.1 SA.4)
Use of `any` typing on req and on the JWT payload (loss of type safety, possible payload-injection of arbitrary fields) is flagged

Mass-assignment risk in PATCH /tickets/:id (spreading req.body directly into the update) is flagged as a Canonical Parsing gap (FIASSE v1.1 S4.4.1.1), with remediation suggesting a typed per-operation schema or field allowlist

DELETE endpoint lacks authorization check (any authenticated user can delete any ticket) is flagged; the report treats authorization as a security feature/requirement rather than as a missing SSEM attribute
JWT verification accepts the token without pinning the algorithm — algorithm-confusion / alg:none risk — is flagged
Authorization filter for non-admins relying on `req.user.email` from a client-controlled JWT payload is flagged as an Isolated Integrity violation (FIASSE v1.1 S4.4.1.2)
Logging gaps and lack of structured audit logging on ticket lifecycle events are flagged under Accountability and/or Observability
Every finding carries a severity and a systemic/local tag, and every expected improvement names the attribute it lifts
Appendix A includes a 50-item checklist (5 per attribute across the ten attributes) with pass/fail markers and a summary count

evals.name: go-http-files-review
evals.prompt: I need an SSEM securability review on this Go file-handling service. Score every attribute, give me the three-part report, and prioritize the issues so I know what to fix first. File is attached.

assertions.text: Output contains the three-part SSEM report (Score Summary / Detailed Findings / Appendix A checklist) with all three parts present
All ten FIASSE v1.1 SSEM attributes each have a numeric 0-10 score, or an explicit 'Not assessed' / 'N/A' marker
Scores show meaningful differentiation across attributes
The overall score is computed as min(raw mean, lowest attribute + 3.0) with the raw mean, floor, binding constraint, and weakest attribute all shown
Path traversal vulnerability in HandleUpload/HandleDownload (filename taken from query string, joined into path with no traversal sanitization) is flagged with specific remediation
Tenant identity taken from a request header (X-Tenant-ID) without authentication or signed-claim verification is flagged as an Isolated Integrity violation (FIASSE v1.1 S4.4.1.2)
Reading the entire upload body with ioutil.ReadAll (no size limit, full buffer in memory) is flagged under Availability and/or Resilience
Use of deprecated ioutil package (and missing context propagation / timeouts) is flagged
Errors propagated raw to the response body via http.Error(w, err.Error(), ...) leaking internal paths is flagged under Resilience (secure failure) and/or Confidentiality
Lack of structured logging (use of fmt.Println) is flagged under Accountability and/or Observability
Recommendations are prioritized, each carrying a severity, a systemic/local tag, and an expected improvement naming the attribute it lifts
Appendix A includes a 50-item checklist (5 per attribute across the ten attributes) with pass/fail markers and a summary count
